subject.title: Feature/docs: end-to-end local voice transcription recipe + transcript cleanup stage (glossary, self-corrections)

question: Should this issue be scoped to documentation for the existing CLI pipeline, or should OpenClaw also own a first-class configurable transcript-cleanup stage?
rationale: The documentation gap is bounded, but a built-in cleanup stage adds configuration, provider/model routing, prompt-security, privacy, failure-policy, and plugin-boundary decisions that cannot be inferred from current behavior.

options.title: Document the existing pipeline
options.body: Add an end-to-end local transcription recipe and a hardened ASR-to-cleanup wrapper example without adding core configuration.

options.title: Sponsor a core cleanup stage
options.body: Define and implement a generic `tools.media.audio.cleanup` contract with upgrade-safe config, security boundaries, failure semantics, docs, and tests.

options.title: Route cleanup externally
options.body: Keep core documentation focused on CLI composition and publish the reusable cleanup implementation as a plugin, skill, or example package through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Document the existing pipeline
recommendation.body: Add an end-to-end local transcription recipe and a hardened ASR-to-cleanup wrapper example without adding core configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to both the media-understanding runtime and the first-party voice-note workflow.
